title: Boards with a shape whose answer follows from plane geometry: clearance, track length and delay, zone area

cases.title: Two parallel tracks 0.25 mm apart edge to edge break a 0.3 mm clearance rule
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: a count, so no difference is accepted
cases.source: IPC-2221 (Generic Standard on Printed Board Design), conductor spacing is the distance between the edges of two conductors; for parallel tracks it is the distance between the centre lines minus the width, here 0.45 - 0.2 = 0.25 mm

cases.title: The measured clearance of the same two tracks
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the geometry is exact in integer nanometres, so one nanometre is wider than needed
cases.source: IPC-2221 conductor spacing as the distance between the edges of two conductors: centre distance 0.45 mm minus the track width 0.2 mm

cases.title: Two parallel tracks 0.35 mm apart edge to edge keep a 0.3 mm clearance rule
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: a count, so no difference is accepted
cases.source: IPC-2221 conductor spacing as the distance between the edges of two conductors: 0.55 - 0.2 = 0.35 mm, above the 0.3 mm limit

cases.title: Length of a straight track along a 3-4-5 triangle scaled to 30 mm by 40 mm
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the length is rounded to the nearest nanometre, so one nanometre is wider than needed
cases.source: Euclid, Elements, book I, proposition 47 (Pythagorean theorem): sqrt(30^2 + 40^2) = 50

cases.title: Delay of that track at the delay of a TEM line in a dielectric of relative permittivity 4
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the settings keep the delay per millimetre in whole femtoseconds, which moves the result by about four parts in 1e5
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, TEM lines: delay = length x sqrt(er)/c, with sqrt(4)/c = 6.671281904 ps/mm over 50 mm

cases.title: Copper area of a 10 mm by 10 mm zone with nothing near it
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the clipping is exact in integer nanometres for a rectangle, so a millionth of a square millimetre is wider than needed
cases.source: Area of a rectangle: 10 mm x 10 mm = 100 mm2

cases.title: Copper area of the same zone with a 0.5 mm track of another net across it and 0.2 mm clearance
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the track and its clearance are cut out as a polygon with sixteen sides per round end, which moves the straight sides by at most 0.2 per cent; half a per cent is wider than that
cases.source: Area of a rectangle minus a strip: 10 x 10 - 10 x (0.5 + 2 x 0.2) = 91 mm2, the strip being the track widened by the clearance on each side and crossing the zone from edge to edge
